Title: Metabolic and genetic response to probiotics supplementation in patients with diabetic nephropathy: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
Author: Mafi et al.
Comment: End-of-treatment values were used as required: placebo 1.4 ± 0.5 and probiotic 1.3 ± 0.5 mg/dL. M_diff was calculated as probiotic minus placebo (1.3 − 1.4 = −0.1 mg/dL) for this simple two-arm comparison; a negative value favors probiotics. The paper reports analysis by ITT with 30 participants per arm despite 27 completers per arm. Arms were identified directly from explicit Table 3 headings; no arm-label inference, unit conversion, or SE-to-SD conversion was required. P = 0.001 is reported for the treatment comparison based on the paper's repeated-measures ANOVA analysis, while this synthesis row uses the unadjusted week-12 arm means and SDs.
Design Type: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel clinical trial; intention-to-treat analysis
Study Environment: Internal clinic and Kashan reference laboratory
Medium: Multi-strain probiotic capsules versus matching starch placebo capsules
Participant type: Patients with diabetic nephropathy and proteinuria
Outcome measurement: Serum creatinine measured using an available commercial kit (Pars Azmun, Tehran, Iran) after an overnight fast
effect_direction: Lower serum creatinine favors probiotics; probiotic-minus-control MD < 0 favors probiotics.

Title: Probiotic supplementation in diabetic hemodialysis patients has beneficial metabolic effects
Author: Soleimani et al.
Comment: M_diff was computed as probiotic minus placebo (7.2 - 7.7 = -0.5 mg/dL) from the explicitly reported week-12 means. No unit or variance conversion was needed.
